articles.title: Watch Reolink recordings on an iPhone
articles.dek: Chrome and Edge gain seeking, while battery cameras join the new playback route.
body: A saved camera clip no longer has to finish downloading before its first picture appears. Home Assistant streams Reolink recordings through a temporary file, letting Safari on iOS request the pieces it needs and letting Chrome and Edge jump to another point in the recording.

The new path replaces the older playback method and also supports recordings from cameras without an HTTP connection, including battery-powered models. Large recordings use temporary disk space rather than filling memory; the files are cleaned up automatically.

pullRequests.title: Use HLS VOD playlist for Reolink recording playback

articles.title: An assistant can work on connections you already have
articles.dek: Administrator tools expose repair notices, discovered devices and sign-in requests; browser authorization still stays with you.
body: An expired sign-in or a discovered device can become a concrete next step for a connected AI assistant. Home Assistant’s management tools list those pending setup tasks alongside translated repair notices, with serious issues placed ahead of lower-priority ones.

Allen Porter also extends the setup tools to change options and reconfigure an existing integration, rather than only create a new connection. The assistant can work through the available forms; an external sign-in step returns a link for the person to finish in Home Assistant.
The repair list is read-only. Seeing a warning does not mean the assistant can resolve every repair automatically, and these system-management capabilities require administrator access.

pullRequests.title: Add options and reconfigure flow support to config LLM tools
Add GetFlowsInProgressTool to config LLM tools
Add GetIssuesTool LLM tool to repairs integration

articles.title: Configure one KNX channel and reuse it for the others
articles.dek: Suggestions can learn from existing controls, including projects without detailed function descriptions.
body: A carefully configured shutter can become the model for other equivalent channels in the same building. Home Assistant reads the existing KNX control’s setup and suggests matching channels, carrying over choices such as inversion and travel times while substituting the correct addresses.

The comparison works across channels on the same device and identically programmed devices. It accepts only unambiguous matches, and channels already using the same addresses are not suggested. The proposal still needs to pass the normal configuration checks; it does not create controls automatically.

A second extension adds thermostat suggestions when the project describes a current temperature and a writable target in the same channel. That route uses standardized device-function descriptions, while copying an existing configuration works without them.

pullRequests.title: Add KNX entity suggestions from existing entity configurations
Add KNX climate suggestions from functional blocks

articles.title: Let LIFX lights follow the music
articles.dek: The new plugin sends colors over the local network and restores the lights after a listening session.
body: A listening session can change compatible LIFX bulbs with the song’s beat and color palette. Music Assistant’s new Lights Sync plugin sends those changes over the local network, saving the lights’ previous state and restoring it afterward.

Each configured lighting group becomes a Sendspin visualizer—a receiver for the music analysis that drives the effects. @sonic1200 makes a first contribution to Music Assistant’s server with the provider; the existing Hue connection is unchanged.

pullRequests.title: Add LIFX Lights Sync plugin provider

articles.title: Plan around rain in the next few minutes
articles.dek: New actions cover Tomorrow.io, Foreca and Belgium’s weather service, with different detail and request costs.
body: An automation can look beyond an hourly forecast before deciding whether to leave something outside. Home Assistant exposes the near-term rain data from three existing weather connections as action responses, rather than adding a ready-made dashboard card.

Tomorrow.io makes its already-fetched short-interval forecast accessible again without another request, skipping intervals that have already ended. Foreca returns the next hour’s precipitation: minute-by-minute radar detail in Europe and the continental United States, and hourly resolution elsewhere. Each Foreca call makes one request.

The Belgian IRM KMI action returns radar predictions in ten-minute steps, or five-minute steps in the Netherlands, with optional earlier frames. It uses cached data and includes the predicted range as well as the rainfall rate.

pullRequests.title: Add get_minute_forecast action to Tomorrow.io
Add get_minute_forecast action to Foreca
Add get_forecasts_radar action to irm_kmi

articles.title: Connect a homemade Thread router by Ethernet
articles.dek: The experimental bridge pauses when its cable is unplugged; it does not move the Thread connection onto Wi-Fi.
body: A Thread device network can reach the home network through a wired ESPHome border router instead of relying on a Wi-Fi link. The new backbone: ethernet option selects that cable connection, with Wi-Fi optional for the board’s own networking.

Border routing stops when the cable connection disappears and starts again when it returns. Ethernet must be enabled at startup; a Wi-Fi fallback for the board itself does not carry the Thread traffic.
The experimental support also admits ESP32-S31 boards with a built-in Thread radio. An ESP32-P4 can host a separate radio, although that combination has only been checked by compiling it.

pullRequests.title: [openthread] Add an Ethernet backbone for border routers

articles.title: Play another room’s wired source on your speaker
articles.dek: The connection stays within its Sonos or HEOS system; some Home Assistant automations need updated source names.
body: A turntable connected to the Den’s Sonos speaker can be selected from the Kitchen instead of only from the speaker beside it. Music Assistant lists the inputs of other speakers in the same system, with the room name attached so listeners can tell them apart.

Sonos shares a connected line-in with the chosen speaker or its group; TV inputs stay with their own speaker. Older Sonos S1 systems only list an input after it has played. HEOS also lists other devices’ inputs, excluding a built-in radio tuner. The listener needs access to the source speaker, and disabled or inaccessible speakers do not supply entries.

HEOS names lose the device prefix: “Den - Line In 1” becomes “Line In 1” on that device. Home Assistant automations selecting the old name need updating. Scripts using Sonos or HEOS input identifiers also need the new identifiers, which are consistent across speakers.

pullRequests.title: Play the input of one Sonos or HEOS speaker on the others

articles.title: Send camera snapshots to your own file server
articles.dek: A new upload action handles several files and creates missing destination folders.
body: A camera automation can save its pictures on a WebDAV server, such as a compatible network storage device. Home Assistant’s upload action accepts one or more local files, including a filename pattern that selects several at once.
Only files inside explicitly allowed local folders can be uploaded. Transfers are streamed in chunks, and the destination folder is created when it does not yet exist.

pullRequests.title: Add WebDAV upload action

articles.title: A filling-level outage stops taking every appliance offline
articles.dek: Optional readings can recover later while the rest of the Miele connection finishes setup.
body: A failing request for appliance filling levels could leave all Miele entities unavailable, even while the service still answered normal device requests. Home Assistant stops making that optional response a condition for starting the integration.

When the readings return, their sensors are added automatically. Bastian Zimmermann makes his first contribution to Home Assistant Core with the correction, tested against both server errors and timeouts.

pullRequests.title: Don't block Miele setup when filling levels can't be fetched

articles.title: A crossed camera boundary can trigger an automation
articles.dek: Compatible ONVIF cameras expose momentary events instead of silently losing them.
body: A line-crossing alert is an instant, not a state that remains on until something clears it. Home Assistant adds event entities for these short-lived camera messages, giving automations a trigger for each new occurrence.
The camera must supply a supported event. Messages repeated when subscribing or renewing the connection are ignored, so reconnecting does not replay an old occurrence as a fresh alert.

pullRequests.title: Add event platform to ONVIF
Document ONVIF event entities

articles.title: Keep Zigbee sensor addresses steady as a device grows
articles.dek: Makers using nRF52 boards can mix fixed and automatic numbering; the eight-function limit remains.
body: Each exposed sensor or control has a numbered address within a Zigbee device. Adding or removing another function could change an automatically assigned number; ESPHome lets makers choose fixed numbers for the functions that need to stay put.

The option covers sensors, binary sensors, numbers and switches on nRF52 boards. Explicit numbers are reserved before the rest are assigned, while unchanged configurations using only automatic numbering keep their existing addresses.
@maniekes makes a first contribution to ESPHome with the feature, tested on an nRF52840 device with Zigbee2MQTT. Sharing one address between several functions is outside this change.

pullRequests.title: [zigbee] Allow explicit endpoint IDs on nRF52

articles.title: Pause ad blocking without forgetting to turn it back on
articles.dek: AdGuard Home handles the return after the duration requested by an automation.
body: A temporary exception no longer needs a separate delayed action to restore protection. Home Assistant adds a timed pause command, and AdGuard Home re-enables its protection when that interval ends.
The existing protection switch remains available for an indefinite on-or-off choice.

pullRequests.title: Add pause protection action to AdGuard Home

articles.title: The story continues after a Deezer audiobook’s intro
articles.dek: The correction affects lossless books whose chapters use a different audio layout from the opening.
body: One Tilda Apfelkern episode played its 36-second theme tune and then ended, with the rest of the book rejected as faulty audio. Music Assistant was reading all chapters using a limit taken from the shorter opening.

Julian Daberkow adjusts the start of the lossless stream so the later chapters can be decoded, and verified that an affected episode plays to the end. MP3 audiobooks and ordinary music tracks keep their existing behavior.

pullRequests.title: Deezer: fix audiobooks stopping after the first chapter

articles.title: North stays north in wind-direction averages
articles.dek: TX20 readings use circular statistics in Home Assistant; the configuration needs no change.
body: Two readings of 350 and 10 degrees both point close to north, but treating them as ordinary numbers puts their average at 180 degrees—south. ESPHome marks TX20 wind direction as an angle so Home Assistant calculates its long-term statistics around the circle.
The change applies to newly calculated statistics and preserves the sensor’s degree unit. It does not change the direction measured by the hardware.
